ledger.note: The Dominion West Loop project serves a gas power plant in Columbiana County, Ohio, and the Dominion project page, the 2019 10-K and EIA rows do not mention data centers.

Kinetik names data centers as a general demand driver, but no source says the Delaware Link pipeline was built for them; a Pecos Power plant interconnection is the only demand link found, with no data center named.
Searches for GTN Xpress with data centers found nothing that names this project.
The Three Rivers Interconnection serves the Three Rivers Energy Center power plant, and the FERC, Enbridge, Alliance and EIA documents do not mention data centers.

A July 2026 Creekstone press release says it bought 43,000 Dth/d of firm Kern River capacity for its Delta data center campus, but it names the Kern River system and not the Delta Lateral, and EIA ties the lateral to the Intermountain Power Project.
Kinder Morgan's June 2026 release and 2025 press coverage tie the Gulf Coast Express expansion to Permian takeaway and South Texas LNG markets, and its data center comments are company-wide.

Williams talks about data center gas demand company-wide and in August 2026 coverage of the Momentum purchase, but no source found says that data centers drive the Louisiana Energy Gateway itself, which serves Gulf Coast LNG.
Williams cited data center demand when buying Momentum, which is the NG3 owner, but sources found describe NG3 as serving LNG, power plants and industry with no data center named for this pipeline.
